newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to sell up to 75pct of state telecom shares.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to sell up to 75pct of state telecom shares.

text.p: Taiwan would sell up to 75 percent of shares in state-owned Chunghwa Telecom Co. in five years, with 20-30 percent being released by early 1999 as part of its privatisation plan, a minister said on Saturday.

"Under our initial plan, we will first sell 20 to 30 percent of shares in Chunghwa Telecom to citizens aged over 20 at the end of 1998 or early 1999," transport and communications minister Tsay Jaw-yang said in a news conference.
Each of these people can apply to buy up to 3,000 shares at a "preferential price", Tsay said, adding his ministry would announce the price after careful calculation.

The state firm would also swap 16 percent to 20 percent of the shares with leading telecom companies overseas, sell five percent to 25 percent of the shares to institutional investors and issue global depository receipts, Tsay said.
Tsay said China Development Corporation -- 10 percent owned by the ruling Nationalist Party -- was working on details of the share release and would come up with a conclusion at the end of October.
Chunghwa, capitalised at T$96.4 billion, was in the process of revaluating its assets, he added.

Before Chunghwa became a company in July 1996, it was a part of the Taiwan government's Directorate General of Telecommunications, which had monopolised the island's telecommunications business for 48 years.
Under reform laws enacted in January 1996, Taiwan liberalised its telecommunications market.
Foreign interests may own 20 percent of Taiwan firms offering phone and data lines services, a ratio designed by parliament to ensure local control of what is considered a strategic resource.
